issues.description: Whether the Board relied on a new ground of refusal (Kashmiri green tea meaning) without fair notice to the applicant; court held no new ground because the examiner never withdrew those refusals.
issues.quote: Because Bayou had a fair opportunity to respond to the examiner's refusals based on the Kashmiri green tea meaning and the examiner never withdrew these refusals, Honeywell, 865 F.3d at 1357, we conclude the Board's genericness and mere descriptiveness findings based on the Kashmiri green tea meaning do not constitute new grounds.

issues.description: Genericness of KAHWA for cafés and coffee shops: court held the Board's genericness finding unsupported by substantial evidence because no record evidence shows cafés sell kahwa.

coding.notes: Reversed the Board's refusal to register KAHWA for cafés and coffee shops; costs to Bayou. Acquired distinctiveness not reached. coding.case_type: Patent: district court and ITC
coding.side_a_parties: ams-OSRAM USA Inc. (fka Texas Advanced Optoelectronic Solutions, Inc. (TAOS))

issues.description: Trade-secret proper accessibility date: whether the secret became properly accessible when it could have been reverse-engineered (Feb. 2005) or when Intersil actually did so (Jan. 2006); court reversed the district court and set the earlier date.
issues.quote: We agree with Intersil and reverse the district court's finding of the proper accessibility date.

issues.description: Trade-secret head-start period: affirmed the district court's finding that the head-start period was 26 months.
issues.quote: We see no clear error in the district court's finding that the relevant duration was 26 months.

issues.description: Disgorgement amount: affirmed inclusion of all ISL29003 profits from iPod Touch sales traceable to the September 2006 design win and the attribution finding against Intersil's challenges.
issues.quote: We therefore affirm the inclusion in the disgorgement award of all profits attributable to Intersil's sales of ISL29003 units to Apple for use in the iPod Touch.

issues.description: TAOS cross-appeal seeking disgorgement of iPhone 3G profits: rejected because the design-win events occurred after the head-start end date.
issues.quote: We therefore reject the cross-appeal and affirm the disgorgement award made by the district court.

issues.description: Intersil's statutory argument that a Texas statute bars exemplary damages was forfeited because it could have been raised in the first appeal.
issues.quote: We hold that it therefore lost the right to make the argument on remand and in this second appeal.

issues.description: Exemplary damages: rejected Intersil's argument that the amount had to be decided by the judge rather than a jury, and its argument that liability and amount were too intertwined for separate factfinders.
issues.quote: In these circumstances, we reject Intersil's challenge to the exemplary-damages award for trade-secret misappropriation.

issues.description: Contract claim: rejected Intersil's double-recovery argument, holding the trade-secret and contract recoveries rested on non-overlapping sales.
issues.quote: It follows that there is no single injury and no double recovery, because the theories of liability arise from two separate and distinct injuries.

issues.description: Contract claim: rejected Intersil's argument that TAOS failed to prove the breach caused the damages (foreseeability under California law).
issues.quote: As TAOS would have reasonably expected to receive compensation for Intersil's use of its confidential information, we see no error in an award of reasonable-royalty damages.

issues.description: Contract claim: upheld reasonable-royalty award on Derivative Products that do not physically incorporate the trade secret, under the breach of confidentiality agreement.
issues.quote: On the evidence, the jury could reasonably include the Derivative Products in the group of sales made as a result of breach and thus award a royalty for those sales.

issues.description: Contract claim: upheld the jury's hypothetical-negotiation finding of a 10-year royalty term as supported by substantial evidence.
issues.quote: We conclude that the jury's royalty finding is supported by substantial evidence.

issues.description: Attorneys' fees: affirmed the award of fees for work on the contract claim under the confidentiality agreement's indemnity clause and California law.
issues.quote: We therefore affirm the district court's award of attorneys' fees.

issues.description: Prejudgment interest: vacated and remanded the start date of interest accrual for sales made after the complaint was filed (Nov. 25, 2008 to June 3, 2014), under Texas and California law.
issues.quote: We vacate the district court's awards of prejudgment interest and remand the case to the district court for further consideration of this issue.

coding.author: Taranto
coding.notes: The underlying dispute is state-law trade-secret misappropriation and breach of contract; the patent claim was dropped before this appeal. No listed case type fits a private-vs-private state-law case, so Patent: district court and ITC was chosen because the case began as a patent suit and the parties align with patent owner and accused infringer. Issues are coded X99 because no P, T, or other substantive code covers Texas or California trade-secret and contract remedies. No judge dissented on any issue.
